text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ruling Party of Democratic Action may decide to run in local elections with some parties in the opposition coalition, including the Party for Bosnia-Herzegovina, led by the co-chairman of Bosnia's Council of Ministers, Haris Silajdzic, political sources say.
- Bosnia's Roman Catholic Cardinal Vinko Puljic urges authorities to ensure refugees can safely return to their homes to prevent sowing the seeds of another conflict.
- The Moslem-Croat Federation's House of Representatives discussed draft laws on formation of municipalities at a session held on Tuesday.
- Both chambers of the central Bosnian parliament are due to convene on Wednesday to discuss the approval of international credits and legal status of Bosnian assembly members.
- Bosnia should become a full-fledged member of the European Council in 1997, says Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic.
- Federation interior ministry denies allegations it planted bombs before Papal visit and says terrorism is on the decline in Bosnia.

- Tuzla canton authorities deny blocking visit of Orthodox Christian Bishop Vasilije Kacavenda to Tuzla, saying he was allowed to travel to Tuzla as an ordinary citizen but not as a state representative.

- A ten-year-old girl is in good condition after undergoing the first open-heart surgery performed in Sarajevo. Another patient, a four-month-old boy, died on Tuesday after post-surgery complications, hospital official sais.
- The office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) announced plans for 200 Croat families to return to their pre-war homes in the Moslem-majority town of Bugojno.
- A pilot project for the return of 100 Moslem families to the Croat-controlled town of Stolac has not been fulfilled, UNHCR says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
